chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa from Ibn Bukayr from Zurara who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married for mut'ah (temporary marriage) without witnesses. He said: There is no objection to the marriage absolutely without witnesses in what is between him and Allah, Exalted and Glorious. And the witnesses were made required in the marriage absolutely only for the sake of the child. And if it were not for that, there would be no objection to it.
ai.seo_question: Is temporary marriage valid without witnesses in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfahar, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the requirement of witnesses in mut'ah is not a condition for the validity of the contract itself (sihha) but rather for the establishment of lineage (nasab) and preventing disputes among offspring. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic view that mut'ah lacks the strict public formalities of permanent marriage, as the union is inherently temporary and focused on the contractual agreement between the parties rather than long-term familial integration.
